chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Ash'ari, from Samakah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, Allah, the Exalted, did not send any Prophet or Imam except that he is the most knowledgeable of the people regarding Allah's affairs.'

He said: 'And He does not command them except with what Allah commands them, nor forbids them except with what Allah forbids them, nor do they assume authority except by Allah's command, nor do they look at each other except by His permission, nor do they speak except with His knowledge, nor do they draw near except through His obedience, nor do they fear except His piety, nor do they hope except for His Paradise, nor do they dread except His Hellfire, nor do they take as allies except His friends, nor do they take as enemies except His enemies.'
He said: 'Whoever contradicts that has contradicted Allah and His Messenger.'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between the commands of the Imams and the commands of Allah?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this hadith to solidify the doctrine of *Ismah* (infallibility), arguing that the Imams' absolute conformity to divine will ensures the preservation of revelation without error. This establishes them not merely as political leaders but as the living, authoritative interpretation of the Quran, a concept central to Twelver Shia jurisprudence and theology.
